upstream_calls: celltypist.annotate(adata, model, mode, p_thres, majority_voting, over_clustering=<obs key>, min_prop) (annotate.py:9)
wrapper_logic: _resolve_model: a string with '/' is a file path; otherwise it is a built-in name, and when that file is absent from the cache only that model is fetched with download_models(model=name) (models.py:474). Without this guard, a bare Model.load(name) on a cache with no .pkl runs download_if_required -> download_models() for all models. A test shows the bare upstream call attempting 61 downloads, while the tool attempts 0.

_h5ad_path: existing .h5ad required. This is a scope restriction: upstream also accepts csv/mtx, but those need upstream's own raw-count normalisation path, which an in-memory AnnData would skip. Documented by the implementer.

limitations: Exactness relies on this machine and these versions: majority voting/Leiden IDs depend on scanpy 1.12.4, igraph 1.0.0 and leidenalg 0.12.0, and seeded training is bit-identical only at the same n_jobs and BLAS threading. Expect small numerical drift and possible cluster relabelling elsewhere; acceptance cases avoid floating-point fields and Leiden-dependent labels except n_over_clusters=20 for demo_400.
The demo_400 Leiden over-cluster count (20) in one acceptance case depends on the same library versions; the scientific tests compare it with the executor reference.
Violin figures are compared structurally and by pixel fraction, not pixel-exactly, because scanpy's strip-plot jitter is random.
Network tests depend on celltypist.cog.sanger.ac.uk; upstream's fixed 30 s download timeout produced one transient failure (see network_checks).
Only .h5ad inputs are exposed (scope choice); csv/mtx inputs and the plain-text over-clustering file of upstream annotate are not exposed.
test_plain_logistic_regression_without_feature_selection takes about 235 s (lbfgs on about 16k genes, run for both the tool and the direct call); the full suite takes about 7.5 min.
